name: RPS-42 radar panel (RADA MHR)
description: S-band AESA panel, one 90 deg face; four panels give 360 deg. Nano-UAS acquisition 3.5 km is published; the 8 km mini-UAS figure has no locatable source and is a planning figure.

detectRangeM.condition: 5000 m against Group 1 (Raven, WASP, Puma class)

rangeAccuracyM.source: RADA RPS-42 brochure as quoted by the radartutorial.eu card and document mirrors; the brochure itself was not opened
rangeAccuracyM.note: Brochure figure for the full 30 km volume-surveillance envelope; coarse next to the short-range C-UAS panels, which is why it sits high in the radar class.

azimuthAccuracyDeg.condition: spatial accuracy <0.5° (one brochure figure for azimuth and elevation; vendor bound taken as 1 sigma)
azimuthAccuracyDeg.source: RADA RPS-42 brochure as quoted by the radartutorial.eu card and document mirrors; the brochure itself was not opened

elevationAccuracyDeg.condition: spatial accuracy <0.5° (one brochure figure for azimuth and elevation; vendor bound taken as 1 sigma)
elevationAccuracyDeg.source: RADA RPS-42 brochure as quoted by the radartutorial.eu card and document mirrors; the brochure itself was not opened

falseAlarmRatePerScan.note: Planning factor: PLACARD_PFA 1e-6 (src/model/types.ts) times about 1e6 range-azimuth-Doppler cells per scan of a 360° surveillance volume gives about one false alarm per scan over the whole coverage; this 90° sector panel searches about half the cells and is recorded at 0.5. No vendor publishes a false-alarm rate.

dwellTimeS.note: Planning factor: Leonardo DRS RADA publishes no dwell or CPI. An electronically scanned radar sets its dwell in the beam schedule rather than by beamwidth over scan rate; the literature CPI of 20 ms for X/Ku-band drone-detection AESAs is used. Open literature on X/Ku-band drone-detection AESAs gives a CPI of about 20 ms at 5 kHz PRF (about 100 pulses; arXiv 2307.10326) and about 30 ms at 6 kHz (about 180 pulses; MDPI Drones 7(5):316), and notes that a 2.7 ms dwell barely resolves micro-Doppler. The MHR datasheet names a software-defined pulse-Doppler AESA with digital beamforming and pulse compression, 60 W average per panel, and no dwell.

pulsesPerDwell.note: Planning factor: Leonardo DRS RADA publishes no PRF or pulse count. 20 ms dwell at the literature 5 kHz PRF gives 100 pulses coherently integrated. Open literature on X/Ku-band drone-detection AESAs gives a CPI of about 20 ms at 5 kHz PRF (about 100 pulses; arXiv 2307.10326) and about 30 ms at 6 kHz (about 180 pulses; MDPI Drones 7(5):316), and notes that a 2.7 ms dwell barely resolves micro-Doppler. The MHR datasheet names a software-defined pulse-Doppler AESA with digital beamforming and pulse compression, 60 W average per panel, and no dwell.
